name: Development and land
answer: These measures show what is being built: the megawatts under construction and planned. For AI data centers the construction pipeline is the earliest sign of where new capacity will come online.

metrics.line: Capacity in permitting, planned, or under construction per market, the standard unit for comparing data center booms across regions.
metrics.label: Construction pipeline in megawatts

reading.body:
The AI data center construction pipeline in this data totals 14,137 megawatts across 42 planned projects, and the ten largest sites alone account for 11,885 of those megawatts.

The pipeline is top-heavy. Meta's Richland Parish project at 5,000 megawatts is more than a third of the entire tracked total, and the top three sites together, Richland Parish, Crusoe Abilene, and CloudBurst San Marcos, come to 7,400 megawatts. Below the top tier the list falls off quickly, from 1,000 megawatts down to entries of 100 to 300 megawatts. That shape matters for AI because a small number of very large campuses will determine how much new compute capacity actually exists, and each one depends on its own power arrangement rather than on a broad grid buildout.

The status notes show how long the gap is between announcement and operation. Richland Parish has been under construction since December 2024 with Entergy's first gas plants not expected online until the end of 2028. Meta's Lebanon project began construction in February 2026 with first buildings expected at the end of 2027. Crusoe Abilene has two buildings operating and six more due by the end of 2026, with an adjacent 900 megawatt Microsoft campus still in site preparation and its first building not expected until mid 2027. The megawatts in this pipeline are years away from serving inference.

What the data does not cover is as important as what it does. It gives capacity figures and, for some entries, construction timelines, but no power contracts, no grid interconnection queue positions, and no indication of whether the electricity to run these sites has been secured. Several entries carry no status at all. The 14,137 megawatts is a statement of intent and early construction, not of capacity that will reliably come online.
